newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-Belgian Solvay rockets on market optimism.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Belgian Solvay rockets on market optimism.

text.p: Shares in Belgian chemicals and drugs company Solvay rocketed more than six percent on Monday, benefiting from a general thirst by European investors for cyclical stocks.

"There is nothing new on the fundamental side but everybody in Europe is seeking industrial companies and more particularly cyclical companies and in Belgium they went for Solvay," one share analyst said.

"We saw that Solvay lagged behind and there was no reason for it as the dollar was rising and chemical prices were up compared to first half of 1996," analyst Jurgen Fryges at KB-Securities told Reuters.
At 1450 GMT Solvay was up 6.55 percent at 21,950 francs after earlier touching an all-time high of 22,000 francs.
"Chemical prices are up, the dollar effect and the acquisition led to the fantastic rise we've seen," Fryges said.
Solvay signed a deal in December to buy 60 percent of Bulgarian soda ash producer SODI SODI SPJS CO for $160 million.

Fryges said KB-Securities had advised their clients to change from "defensive shares" -- banks, insurance companies and utility companies -- to cyclical stocks because of the evolution in the economy.
"The acquisition was more or less a turning point to look more closely to Solvay...and once it was at 20,000 everything went quite quickly," he added.
"I don't think Solvay will now have a setback or lag behind I think it will have a strong year this year," he said.

Analysts said Solvay's pharmaceutical activities were also a reason for the increased attention on the stock, but they added that the results of Solvay's pharmaceutical products would not show through in the short term.
Fryges said Solvay was developing two or three drugs against schizophrenia and anxiety.
Brussels-based Solvay has a workforce of 38,000 people. Total sales in 1995 were $9.3 billion.
